reviewer_reports.summary: The diff adds benchmark fixtures, canned review data, metadata, and release records. I did not find a correctness or security issue in the product code changes themselves that is supportable from this diff.
I found one correctness issue in the new bench harness that can silently produce duplicate or conflicting scores for the same case after a config rename or alias change.

findings.title: Resume logic keys prior results by stored config name instead of the current output file
findings.evidence: 'done = {(r['config'], r['case_id']) for r in records}' and later 'key = (cfg['name'], case['id'])'
findings.recommendation: When resuming from '<out>/<config>.jsonl', treat every retained record in that file as belonging to the current config file regardless of its embedded 'config' field, or normalize retained records to 'cfg['name']' before building 'done'. Otherwise a config rename or alias change with identical 'config_sha256' will bypass deduplication and append a second record for the same case into the same results file.

reviewer_reports.summary: The new benchmark corpus manifest is internally inconsistent with the files added in this diff. That will break any loader that validates the manifest against on-disk case directories, which the new docs explicitly say it does.

findings.title: Benchmark docs promise manifest validation, but the added manifest references many missing case directories
findings.evidence: '(the loader refuses a corpus whose manifest and directories disagree).'
findings.recommendation: Either add all case directories referenced by `bench/corpus/manifest.json` in this change, or trim the manifest to only the cases actually present. Also add a test that loads the shipped corpus from disk so this mismatch cannot regress.

findings.title: Corpus manifest lists case ids that are not added in this patch, making the shipped corpus invalid

findings.recommendation: Make `bench/corpus/manifest.json` match the actual contents of `bench/corpus/` in this release, or include the missing case directories and files in the patch. A corpus self-check in CI should verify every manifest id has both `case.json` and `diff.patch`.

reviewer_reports.summary: The diff adds a dispositions file summarizing review-v12 findings and their resolutions; all code changes in the diff are either documentation or already-rebutted findings with fixes applied. No new reliability risks are introduced.

The new agent timeout plumbing has a correctness regression: explicitly passing 0 or another falsey timeout value is ignored and replaced with the default. I did not find a diff-supported security issue beyond that.

findings.title: Falsey agent_timeout values are silently replaced with the default
findings.evidence: 'command, timeout=agent_timeout or AGENT_TIMEOUT,'
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit None check so only an omitted timeout falls back to the default, e.g. compute 'timeout = AGENT_TIMEOUT if agent_timeout is None else agent_timeout' before calling command_agent.

reviewer_reports.summary: The diff adds changelog, README, bench infrastructure, and test coverage for the v0.9.1 release; all changes are consistent with the adjudicated v12 findings and the enumeration test validates every build_providers/build_solvers path. No new reliability or safety issues are introduced.
The diff introduces a release-record verification bypass for private-repo policy and a correctness regression in fixture path matching that can misclassify unrelated files as fixtures.

findings.title: Record verification does not enforce the private-repo free-tier policy
findings.evidence: 'known = {r.get('family') for r in ok_reports' ... 'add('two_families', len(known) >= 2,' ... 'return {'eligible': all(c['ok'] for c in checks),'
findings.recommendation: Extend 'verify_record' to validate the recorded seat tiers against the repository privacy policy, e.g. fail eligibility when any successful reviewer report has tier 'free' for a private repository, or record and verify an explicit 'private' flag in the report.

findings.title: Plain fixture paths match sibling prefixes and can hide non-fixture findings
findings.evidence: 'base = pat.rstrip('/')' and 'if path == base or path.startswith(base + '/'):'
findings.recommendation: For plain paths, distinguish files from directories instead of treating every pattern as a directory prefix. Match exact file paths only, and only apply prefix matching when the manifest explicitly denotes a directory such as with a trailing slash or '/**'.

reviewer_reports.summary: The diff only adds tests, and I did not find a correctness or security issue introduced by these additions that is supportable from the diff itself.

The diff adds a comprehensive test suite (test_v091_fixes.py) covering timeout enumeration, forwarding, validation, bench force rerun, fixture inner paths, and subprocess ordering — all aligned with the v12 closure criteria. No production code changes are present; the change is purely test infrastructure that enforces the guards the v12 panel documented. All cited findings from the prior round are either fixed, rebutted, or recorded as repeats with mechanisms. The new tests provide executable ev

The diff introduces robust agent isolation, timeout handling, retryable error classification, cross-kind seat-name collision detection, and a full test suite covering the new functionality. No blockers, majors, or minors were found; only a nit regarding the unused `re` import.

reviewer_reports.summary: The diff introduces a race-condition vulnerability (check-then-act) and a read-modify-write counter race in benchmark corpus files; these are intentional defect-injection fixtures but must be flagged per the operations & reliability lens.

findings.title: Check-then-act race: existence check and create are not atomic
findings.evidence: if not os.path.exists(path):\n    return open(path, "w")\nraise FileExistsError(path)
findings.recommendation: Replace the non-atomic check-then-act pattern with an atomic file creation (os.open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL) or use a lock to ensure the existence check and creation happen without a gap.

findings.title: Read-modify-write counter races under concurrent requests
findings.evidence:
count = store.get(f"views:{page_id}") or 0
store.set(f"views:{page_id}", count + 1)

def record_click(store, page_id):
    count = store.get(f"clicks:{page_id}") or 0
    store.set(f"clicks:{page_id}", count + 1)
findings.recommendation: Use an atomic increment operation provided by the store (e.g., INCR in Redis) or add a threading lock around the read-modify-write cycle.

The change is sound under the operations & reliability lens.
